stories.author: paavohtl
stories.title: Rust project goals: Immobile types and guaranteed destructors
stories.groq_label: Types will be allowed to opt out of being moved or forgotten.
stories.groq_discussion:
Discussion type: – Detailed:

This Rust project aims to solve the problem of immobile types and guaranteed destructors. The Hacker News discussion suggests that commenters were primarily interested in understanding the implications and potential applications of this feature. They explored the idea of immobile types, which would allow for the creation of cyclical referenced types without using reference cycles, currently not detectable by the compiler. Commenters also discussed how this is related to the safety of Rust's `mem::forget` function and how it could be safely used to leak values.

Regarding algebraic effects being retrofitted onto Rust, commenters appreciated the potential of this feature to support useful patterns in async Rust programming. They highlighted the promise of this development, although many emphasized the need for a clear explanation of how this would work for someone new to async Rust programming. Overall, the discussion indicates that the project's introduction of immobile types and guaranteed destructors could introduce a new dimension to Rust programming, although its long-term success would depend on how it interacts with existing features.
stories.groq_explain: Rust is changing its type system to make it more flexible and allow for certain features that are currently not possible, such as self-referential types and types that need to run their own destructors.
